slides.title: Why your espresso tastes bitter
slides.subtitle: It's not the coffee. It's what the water kept taking.

slides.title: Water takes flavor in order
slides.body: Brewing is dissolving. Acids and sweetness come out first. Bitter compounds come out later. Stop too early and it tastes sour. Run too long and it turns bitter.
slides.highlight: Bitter usually means too much extraction.

slides.title: Cause one: the grind is too fine
slides.body: Finer grounds expose more surface and slow the water down. More contact time means more extraction, and past a point, more bitterness.

slides.title: Cause two: water finds a shortcut
slides.body: Water can crack through the puck, the packed coffee in the basket. This is called channeling. The cracks get over-extracted while the rest is barely touched.

slides.caption: A common starting range for a shot. It depends on your coffee: taste and adjust.

slides.label: The tip
slides.body: Shot running slow and bitter? Grind a little coarser. Change one thing at a time, then taste.

slides.title: Bitter means the water stayed too long
slides.body: Grind a bit coarser, keep the puck even, and taste.
slides.cta: Save this for your next shot
